(mainly found within and beneath the skin)
helps keep the duck buoyant.  Duck is also
rich in protein.  It is an excellent source of
riboflavin, niacin, and phosphorus and is
a good source of iron, zinc, and thiamin.
Duck’s reputation as scrawny may be unde-
served, however.  They do have a large
skeleton and thus a relatively high propor-
tion of bone.  But specialty breeds, such as
Muscovy ducks, have increased breast size
for more meat.  The USDA grades duck
quality with classifications A, B, and C,
similar to other poultry.
